title: Emergent model entrant early-warning & opportunity index
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: New open and commercial LLM entrants appear frequently and can impact Redwood's model catalog availability, cost, and competitive positioning. PM, research, and sales need a low-friction mechanism to detect high-impact entrants early and surface actionable opportunities (e.g., low-cost inference, unique capability, enterprise-friendly licenses).

Goal: Build an index that scores emergent model entrants on threat/opportunity dimensions and produces prioritized alerts and suggested next steps for: model onboarding prioritization, pricing/route adjustments, and go-to-market collateral.

Scope: This ticket covers the product definition, signal taxonomy, prototype scoring heuristics, and a light-weight dashboard + alerting rules for trialing with the Competitive Intelligence and Applied ML teams. It does NOT include full integration into the Console or automated provisioning.

Success metrics: 
- Precision@10 for high-impact alerts >= 0.7 (manual review by PM + ML reviewer)
- Time from public model release to triaged alert <= 72 hours for top-20% signals
- At least 3 actionable opportunities surfaced in pilot (cost arbitrage, unique capability, enterprise license)

Deliverables: 
1) Signal taxonomy document (sources, signal weightings, freshness heuristics)
2) Scoring prototype (spreadsheet + reproducible notebook) that ingests: GitHub PRs/releases, model hub release feeds, provider announcements, Twitter/X thread extractions, and community benchmark results.
3) Lightweight dashboard mock (Confluence + clickthrough Figma) showing ranked entrants, signal breakdown, and recommended next actions.
4) Pilot runbook and manual triage checklist for CI and Applied ML teams.
acceptance_criteria: Taxonomy doc reviewed by Applied ML and CI docs owners
Prototype spreadsheet reproduces scores for 5 historical entrants
Dashboard mock approved by Head of Product
Pilot runbook and triage checklist published
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with CI, Applied ML, and Sales. Agreed narrow pilot scope: open-model releases + provider announcements only.
2026-03-05: Research found three high-noise sources (X threads, Discord chatter, and some model hub PRs). Decided to apply frequency dampening and novelty boosts.
2026-03-08: Prototype scoring spreadsheet ingests model card metadata and GitHub release notes. Early weighting favors permissive licenses and low parameter counts for cost-opportunity signals.
2026-03-10: Shared Confluence draft. CI requested a 'customer-exposure' tag to mark entrants likely to be adopted by existing customers. Added to taxonomy.
2026-03-12: Figma dashboard mock uploaded; scheduled review with Head of Product 2026-03-16. Next work: formalize precision evaluation dataset and run historical backtest for 12 entrants.
